newsitem.title: EGYPT: Islamist group says Algerian under house arrest.
newsitem.headline: Islamist group says Algerian under house arrest.

text.p: An exiled Moslem militant group said on Sunday Algerian authorities had put under house arrest a woman detained by Egypt on suspicion of aiding the violent Jihad group, which is seeking to overthrow the Cairo government.

The Islamic Observation Centre said in a faxed statement that the Egyptian authorities deported Algerian Djamila al-Falaki and two of her children last Wednesday after detaining her for almost one month.

Falaki was arrested by the Algerian authorities as soon as she landed and taken to an unknown destination where she was mistreated and interrogated, the group said. She was released on Saturday in a "worrying" physical and psychological state and taken to her home where she is under house arrest, it added.
"We don't know why she was subjected to this...as the country that levied charges against her released her due to lack of evidence," the statement said.
"We call on human rights organisations to support the Algerian cause, the cause of Djamila al-Falaki and her children and the cause of all those who are oppressed," it added.

In March, the Egyptian interior ministry said police had arrested Falaki with money, a firearm and literature of the Jihad group in her possession. It said she had tried to contact three lawyers who were members of the group, which assassinated president Anwar Sadat in 1981.

But prominent fugitive militant Yasser Serri, who is close to the Islamic Observation Centre, said that he had not recruited Falaki. Egypt has said Serri is a Jihad member on the run from several jail terms in Egypt and a death sentence for trying to kill prime minister Atef Sedki in 1993.

Jihad is one of several militant groups fighting to topple the Egyptian government and set up a strict Islamic state. More than 1,000 people have been killed in political violence since militants began their anti-government campaign in 1992.
